classification: Retained local implementation verification or independent assessment; not production configuration or formal gate passage

findings.title: Prior-review export can exceed the current repository scope
findings.regressionSetup: Create an app-plus-service prior review, then select an app-only current candidate and reference that prior report. Assert the evaluator view excludes prior service source. The read-only probe extracted the exact reviewerView function and used in-memory mkdir/writeFile substitutes recording destinations; both app/app.js and service/private-service.js were observed.
findings.observed: Out-of-scope historical repository source copied into reviewer view.
findings.remedy: Validate history and delta repository scope before execution; reject incompatible references or construct a bounded permitted history view.

findings.title: Affected closed findings require no renewed disposition
findings.regressionSetup: Supply a prior code result with blocking finding f1 at app/app.js, a later resolved disposition for f1, and a current change to app/app.js. Submit a PASS verdict covering app/app.js and interactions with empty findings and dispositions. The read-only probe of the exact validateVerdict function accepted it. Also test automatic history selection without manually resubmitting f1.
findings.observed: PASS accepted without a disposition for an affected previously closed finding.
findings.remedy: Automatically select conservatively affected closures and require independent dispositions; carry unaffected closures through justified applicability without requiring every historical ID.

findings.title: Fresh evidence cannot recover a missing historical artifact
findings.regressionSetup: Produce passing retained proof, remove an old output blob, then produce complete fresh self-contained proof. Verify the old loss remains visible but current proof can restore applicability. Separately remove an old result JSON and verify repair execution remains available. This finding is source-derived; no destructive probe was performed.
findings.observed: Unconditional closure of all historical results prevents fresh-proof recovery; missing historical result JSON can prevent execution.
findings.remedy: Preserve visible lost history and introduce an explicit recovery record permitting fresh proof to replace current applicability without fabricating, overwriting, or reconstructing old proof from current bytes.

findings.title: Provider failures expose raw provider output in ordinary result summaries
findings.regressionSetup: Call runAgentProcess with a local Node process that prints RAW_PROVIDER_CONTEXT_SENTINEL to stderr and exits 1. The probe observed that sentinel verbatim in error.message. Exercise gate execution failure to ensure its normal summary and UI exclude raw stdout/stderr.
findings.observed: Provider stderr appears verbatim in exceptions that current execution persists and surfaces as summaries. No real secret leak was asserted.
findings.remedy: Use bounded structured error categories and sanitized summaries; handle necessary diagnostics separately.

findings.title: Supported host interception capability and applicable hook smoke are not established
findings.regressionSetup: Determine interception capabilities for supported host versions. For applicable supported hooks, demonstrate invocation of the same core and denial of invalid passage; otherwise document the demonstrated unavailable capability.
findings.observed: Evidence establishes SessionStart guidance and unconfigured action hooks rather than host capability or an applicable action-hook smoke. No observed bypass is claimed.
findings.remedy: Supply capability determination and applicable supported-hook evidence.

rubric.assessment: `current/core.js:117–188,260–322` checks approved commitments, specification validation, scoped authority and milestone proof. Tests `50–58,116–126,283–309,413–425` exercise refusal and integration/completion. Corrective execution remains separately available.

Readiness only records an event (`core.js:183–188`); execution is explicit (`execution.js:210–241`). No round counter or cross-gate scheduling graph is imposed. Tests `61–68` repeat readiness seven times without review launch.

`current/adapter.js:11–26` uses the canonical resolver; evidence storage does not require Git ownership. Tests `71–78,235–248,283–309,480–515,529–537` cover repository-local, shared parent, tracked/ignored parent records, and combined repositories.

`current/evidence.js:17–61,83–129` retains exact Git blobs and raw requirements with scope and authority references. `core.js:223–258` checks current applicability. Tests cover changed requirements/source, combined repositories and identical-content commits. Export containment fails separately under R5.
Path traversal/symlink protections exist (`current/store.js:10–49`), but prior source export exceeds current repository scope. Finding 1.
Exclusive publication and hash verification are implemented (`store.js:65–108,223–242`). Missing historical artifacts cannot recover through fresh proof as permitted by C4. Finding 3.

Packet inventory and local reference closure are core-derived (`execution.js:428–438`); application cleanliness remains enforced (`evidence.js:73–95`). Test `283–309` completes the intact-evidence path without evidence commits. The historical-loss recovery defect is scored under R6.

Separate verdict validation and receipt qualification are implemented (`execution.js:91–128,343–353`; tests `180–200`). Actual fresh Claude execution is retained in `verification/live-evaluator.json`. However, the row also requires input isolation, which Finding 1 violates.

`current/contracts.js:40–54` retains context, reconciliation, Verification, spec, pattern, independent Judge, code review, triage, explanation, packet, finalization, release, retention and optional whiteboard. Runner proof comes from actual subprocess receipts (`execution.js:130–161`).

Content identity excludes commit IDs while retaining relevant source content (`evidence.js:108–112`); reuse preserves original references (`execution.js:299–318`). Tests `165–178,517–526` establish reuse and original provenance.

Source/requirements, consumed proof, support documents, dependency inputs, declared environment and external validity are checked (`core.js:239–256`; `current/environment.js:36–54`). Tests `223–232,372–380,446–459,480–500,578–589` cover important mutations. Environment completeness remains dependent on declared assumptions.

Prior qualifying proof, unchanged requirements/criteria, changed paths, interactions and coverage are required (`execution.js:203–205,273–283`; `core.js:249–254`). Tests `202–220,501–514` include combined-repository coverage rejection. Affected finding disposition remains defective under R13.
Claims and history are bounded and separated, but affected closures can be omitted or accepted without disposition. Finding 2.
Instructions permit new instances and distinguish advice; blocking findings require approved criteria or the gate rule (`execution.js:44–50,171–176`). Test `218–220` retains a new blocking result.

`current/contracts.js:62–87` records actual available provenance and named continuations; `core.js:134–161,338–349` handles amendments and repeat reconciliation. Tests `312–340` preserve old/new commitments and avoid duplicate passage.

Waivers remain separate from verdicts and are candidate-scoped (`contracts.js:89–93`; `core.js:297–310`). Integration is independently observed (`actions.js:93–113`). Tests `116–126,342–350,462–477` preserve failed outcomes and reject inferred authority.

Protected adapter checks and branch-direction fixtures are supported. The supplied matrix establishes configured behavior, but does not establish supported host interception capability or exercise an applicable action hook.
CLI, native adapter and desktop use the current core; incidental ordering controls are removed. Provider errors nevertheless expose raw output through summaries. Finding 4.

`source/plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/index.js:1–12` exports the current interface; the CLI current command set and native adapter route to it. Old merge entry is explicitly retired in `source/plugin-src/shared/resources/scripts/pr_lifecycle.py:159`. No pilot or benchmark admission requirement was found.

`core.js:72–110` establishes current runs without interpreting old journals; `store.js:135–185` durably establishes activation successors. Tests `93–101,326–340,560–576` cover preserved history, repeated entry and damaged/unsupported runs.

Receipts retain timing, identity and outcomes, with unavailable token/cost metrics represented as null (`execution.js:384–389`). `verification/real-project-observation.md:3–14` provides the requested observation recipe without adding an adoption gate.

limitations: Only frozen candidate, approved requirements and supplied verification were evaluated.
Full suites were not independently rerun; reported suite results were inspected from supplied logs.
Three additional probes were read-only function/subprocess checks; in-memory filesystem substitutes were used where necessary.
No candidate installation, network access or source mutation was performed during evaluation.
Missing-historical-artifact finding is source-derived, not a destructive runtime probe.
R17 is an evidence gap rather than a claimed observed host-hook bypass.
Source-commit metadata names starting HEAD, not uncommitted candidate release identity.
This is not formal installed-protocol passage.
